acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Wolves family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Howler, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Pack-Tempo Specialist archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Tall narrow-chested wolf with a large pale throat ruff, deep rib cage, long muzzle, and a visibly working throat cavity.
Signature mechanic: Directed Howl: one directional howl releases the indicated wing while every Wolf on the opposite side pauses and braces.
battlefieldDuty: Change the pack's attack rhythm by advancing allies on one side while the opposite wing holds position.
constructionDimensions: Coat, hide, claws, breath, saliva, scars, and dust remain physically ordinary and retain species-specific coloration.
Pack motion is expressed through compressed shoulders, paw placement, tail alignment, and disturbed terrain without supernatural residue.
counterplay: Interrupt the inhale or cross through the temporarily stationary wing before the advancing side closes. Affinity signal: The committed shoulder, crossed forepaw, expanded throat ruff, scent line, or rising hackles remain fully visible before the associated attack.
forbiddenTreatments: Elemental glow or unexplained magical anatomy
Humanoid posture, hands, clothing, saddles, or manufactured armor
identityInvariants: Every form retains a four-legged lupine skeleton, long muzzle, visible paws, expressive ears, and a readable tail; no form becomes humanoid or wears manufactured armor.
Rank is communicated through chest mass, coat mantle, scars, posture, and pack behavior rather than arbitrary glow or simple scale.
Pack attack direction remains readable through gaze, ear position, tail line, paw placement, and the spacing of companion Wolves.
telegraph: Its pale throat ruff expands and its muzzle points directly toward the wing that will advance.
